**No code fix is warranted. The correct action is a stand-down no-op.**

The tick-49 audit is a *clean idle audit*: every autonomous gate passes — build/vet PASS, 11/11 pkgs green, golangci 0 issues, gofmt clean, gitreins guard PASS + 10/10 complete, CI ci-workflow GREEN (run 30788361932), Hilo fresh, no new issues, no remote commits, deps only transitive-minor.

The single red item, **DOCKER-GHCR-001 `blocked-human` unchanged**, is by definition non-actionable: it is an external/credential/ownership blocker that has not changed since prior ticks, and retrying it would violate the confirmed 7200s cooldown discipline (scheduler API verified, no PUT issued). Fabricating a commit or "fix" here would be the actual defect — the idle audit's job is to detect *when not to act*.

The fix this tick implements is the no-op policy itself. Illustrative gate (what an idle-audit tick should execute; no repo change was made):

```go
// Action decides what a tick must do, in priority order.
// Cooldown always wins: it prevents thrashed retries of known blockers.
type Audit struct {
    CooldownRemaining time.Duration
    BuildOK, VetOK, GofmtClean, GuardOK, CIGreen bool
    LintIssues int
    DockerBlocked bool // human-blocked, non-actionable
}

func (a Audit) Action() string {
    switch {
    case a.CooldownRemaining > 0:
        return "noop:cooldown" // 7200s confirmed via scheduler API; do NOT PUT
    case !a.BuildOK || !a.VetOK || !a.GofmtClean || a.LintIssues > 0:
        return "fix:code"
    case !a.GuardOK:
        return "fix:gitreins"
    case !a.CIGreen:
        return "fix:ci"
    case a.DockerBlocked:
        return "noop:blocked-human(DOCKER-GHCR-001)" // escalate, never retry
    default:
        return "noop:idle" // tick 49: this branch; emit no commit
    }
}
```

Applied to tick 49: `Action() == "noop:idle"` — zero commits, zero dependency bumps (transitive-minor only), zero docker retries, zero issue mutations.
